question: Are hallmarking charges based on jewellery weight?
answer: No. Hallmarking charges are paid per article, irrespective of the article's weight.

question: Are product-specific technical guidelines available?
answer: Yes. BIS Product Manuals are available for certified products. They include sampling guidelines, test-equipment lists, Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), product scope and related technical requirements.

question: Are separate applications needed for different brands manufactured at the same location?
answer: No. The application is for the product at a manufacturing premise. The firm must provide an undertaking and relevant documents concerning the brand name.

question: Are technical manuals available for FMCS applicants?
answer: Yes. Product Manuals and Schemes of Inspection and Testing are available for many Indian Standards and provide information such as infrastructure, SIT and sampling requirements.

question: Are there Government regulations specifically governing hallmarking?
answer: Yes. The BIS (Hallmarking) Regulations, 2018 were notified on 14 June 2018.
document_reference: BIS Act and Regulation FAQ Q2

question: Can a BIS licensee participate in standards formulation/revision?
answer: Yes. A BIS licensee can participate by becoming a member of the relevant technical committee and may submit comments to the concerned BIS technical department.

question: Can a common person get hallmarked jewellery tested for purity at an A&H Centre?
answer: Yes. A consumer can get hallmarked jewellery/sample tested at a BIS-recognized A&H Centre after paying the applicable testing charge. BIS states ₹200 for testing by fire assay according to IS 1418.

question: Can a test report issued to an IEC or another international standard be accepted?
answer: No. The FMCS FAQ states that only the test report according to the relevant Indian Standard is accepted.

question: Can an A&H Centre refuse jewellery because of workload?
answer: No. The centre should not refuse to accept jewellery. It may inform the jeweller that testing will be delayed, and it should follow the First In, First Out (FIFO) principle.

question: Can an A&H Centre return jewellery that does not match the purity or weight declared by the jeweller?
answer: Yes. The A&H Centre can return jewellery that does not conform to the declared purity or weight details.

question: Can an artisan or common person directly approach an A&H Centre for hallmarking?
answer: No. Only BIS registered/certified jewellers can approach an Assaying & Hallmarking Centre for hallmarking jewellery.

question: Can an importer apply for a BIS licence on behalf of the foreign manufacturer?
answer: No. Under FMCS, the application must be made by the foreign manufacturer itself.

question: Can FMCS fees be paid in USD or INR?
answer: For SAARC countries, payment may be made in USD or INR with GST. For other countries, payment is required in USD.

question: Can I change the scope of an existing BIS product licence?
answer: Yes. Varieties may be included or deleted through the applicable Change in Scope of Licence procedure and relevant guidelines.

question: Can I obtain a BIS licence if a Product Manual/SIT/grouping guideline/marking-fee rate is not available?
answer: Yes. A first manufacturer may still obtain a BIS licence under Scheme-I. BIS interacts with the applicant to establish product-specific guidelines and marking-fee rates; this is treated as an All India First Licence situation.

question: Can inspection samples be tested at any ILAC/APLAC laboratory or government laboratory in the manufacturer's country?
answer: No. Samples drawn during BIS inspection must be tested at BIS laboratories or BIS-recognized laboratories. Samples drawn by BIS are sent to a laboratory in India by the applicant firm, and the applicant bears actual testing charges.

question: Can jewellery failing the declared purity be hallmarked at the immediately lower grade?
answer: No. The jewellery must be rejected and returned to the jeweller.

question: Can Off-Site Centres operate in mandatory-hallmarking districts?
answer: Yes. BIS states that an Off-Site Centre can also be established in districts covered under mandatory hallmarking.

question: Can old jewellery be sold after hallmarking becomes mandatory?
answer: Yes. Consumers can sell old hallmarked or unhallmarked jewellery to jewellers.

question: Can one application cover different products and IS standards manufactured at the same factory?
answer: No. A separate application is required for each product and Indian Standard even when they are manufactured at the same factory location.

question: Can one application cover the same product manufactured at different factories?
answer: No. A separate application is required for every factory location, even when the product and Indian Standard are the same.

question: Can one application cover the same product manufactured at different locations?
answer: No. A separate application is required for each product/IS and each manufacturing location.

question: Can one BIS licence be used for every variety of a product made in the factory?
answer: No. A licence is granted for one product/Indian Standard and may cover multiple varieties, grades or sizes only to the extent they are included in the licence scope. The Standard Mark cannot be used on varieties outside that approved scope.

question: Can one FMCS application cover different products/IS standards made at the same factory?
answer: No. A separate application is required for each product/Indian Standard for each factory location.

question: Do hallmarking charges include making charges or wastage?
answer: No. Hallmarking charges do not include making charges or wastage charges.

question: Does BIS conduct surveillance after granting a licence?
answer: Yes. BIS conducts surprise factory surveillance inspections to verify that manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, QC and testing capabilities continue to be maintained. Factory testing may be witnessed, samples may be drawn for third-party laboratory testing, and market surveillance may also be carried out.

question: Does the AIR have to be an Indian resident?
answer: Yes. The AIR should be an Indian national and resident of India. A foreign national may qualify if employed by an Indian office/branch of the manufacturer and residing in India.

question: For which products is a BIS licence mandatory?
answer: BIS licensing is mandatory for products covered under the applicable compulsory-certification/QCO list.

question: How can a consumer file a hallmarking complaint?
answer: The consumer can first approach the jeweller for compensation if retesting at a BIS-recognized A&H Centre establishes lower-than-declared purity. A complaint can also be made to BIS, which investigates the complainant and accused side, including jeweller and A&H Centre, before taking action under applicable law and regulations.

question: How can I find the Indian Standard for my product if I do not know the IS number?
answer: Search for the Indian Standard corresponding to the product through Manakonline. If the relevant standard cannot be found, the manufacturer may contact the concerned BIS technical department.

question: How do I apply for a BIS licence under FMCS?
answer: The foreign manufacturer submits the prescribed application with the required FMCS documents and fees. Current BIS guidance allows online FMCS applications through Manakonline; from 1 June 2026, only online applications are accepted.

question: How do I renew my BIS licence?
answer: Renewal is requested online through the Manakonline dashboard. The renewal application must include production details for the relevant period for marking-fee calculation and the applicable renewal fee.

question: How does a consumer register a BIS complaint?
answer: Complaints may be submitted offline or online through the BIS Care App, the BIS online complaint portal or by email to the BIS complaints address.

question: How does an A&H Centre obtain recognition?
answer: An assaying centre meeting IS 15820:2009 requirements for gold/silver jewellery/artefacts must apply online through Manakonline. BIS grants recognition after verifying infrastructure, quality-management system and trained/competent manpower.

question: How does BIS grant a product-certification licence?
answer: BIS assesses manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities through a visit to the manufacturing premises. Product conformity is established through third-party laboratory testing, testing at the manufacturing premises or a combination of both.

question: How does BIS registration/certification benefit a jeweller?
answer: It provides an indication of capability, evidence of commitment to quality and assurance of consistency in gold/silver jewellery purity and quality.

question: How does the digital hallmarking system help prevent fraudulent hallmarking?
answer: The system records date/time stamps of assaying and hallmarking activities and uses a unique six-digit HUID that can be traced to the jeweller and A&H Centre. Consumers can verify HUID through the BIS Care App.

question: How long does FMCS licensing normally take?
answer: BIS states that average grant time is generally six months from receipt and recording of a complete application. The period can vary because of queries, inspections, sample transportation and outstanding payments.

question: How long does it take to obtain a BIS product-certification licence?
answer: BIS states an average grant time of about one month under Option-2 and four months under Option-1, calculated from receipt and recording of a complete application. Actual time can vary due to queries, inspection, sample deposition and fee/payment issues.

question: How long is a Scheme-I BIS licence valid?
answer: A Scheme-I licence may initially be granted for up to two years and is valid only for the varieties included in the licence scope. Renewal may extend the licence up to five years from its last validity date, subject to applicable requirements and fees.

question: How long is an FMCS BIS licence valid?
answer: The FAQ states that BIS certification under Scheme-I may initially be granted for up to two years after payment of advance minimum marking fee. It covers only the varieties included in the licence and may be renewed up to five years from the last validity date, subject to requirements.

question: How many Off-Site Centres can one A&H Centre establish?
answer: A maximum of five Off-Site Centres may be set up within a 100 km radius by each parent A&H Centre having a fire-assay laboratory in districts not covered under mandatory hallmarking.

question: How old can a test report be for Option-2?
answer: Product test reports should generally not be more than 90 days old, subject to the detailed Grant of Licence guidelines.

question: Is a BIS licence mandatory for importing products into India?
answer: BIS certification is generally voluntary, but products notified by the Government under QCOs may be imported into India only when the required Standard Mark/certification conditions are satisfied.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for my product?
answer: BIS certification is compulsory for products brought under compulsory certification by the Central Government under the BIS Act, 2016 or another applicable Act. A product appearing in BIS's compulsory-certification list requires BIS certification as applicable.

question: Is hallmarking covered by the BIS Act, 2016?
answer: Yes. Hallmarking is covered under the BIS Act, 2016.
document_reference: BIS Act and Regulation FAQ Q1

question: Is nomination of an Authorized Indian Representative mandatory?
answer: Yes. A foreign applicant must nominate an Indian-resident Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) when applying.

question: Must both articles in a pair be hallmarked?
answer: Yes. Each article in a pair must have its own hallmark and a different HUID.

question: Must detachable parts of jewellery be hallmarked?
answer: Yes. All detachable parts should have separate hallmarking with different HUIDs.

question: Q 1 What is a licence?
answer: Licence means a licence granted under Section 13 of BIS Act 2016 to use a specified Standard Mark in relation to any goods or article which conforms to a standard.

question: Q.10 Can I submit one application for different products and Indian Standards(ISS) being manufactured at the same factory location?
answer: No, separate application for each product and ISS is required to be submitted even for same factory location.

question: Q.11 Can I submit one application for same product being manufactured at different factory locations?
answer: No, separate application for each factory location is required to be submitted, even if the product and ISS is same.

question: Q 12: Which are the laboratories of which test report will be acceptable to BIS for the purpose of grant of licence? Or Where can I get my products tested in order to get a licence under optionv- 2?
answer: The test reports which are issued by only BIS or BIS recognized or empanelled laboratory for the product are acceptable for grant of a licence under option-2. To know details of laboratory for testing of a particular product, please visithttp://164.100.105.198:8096/bis_access/iswise_v2.html

question: Q 13. Up to how much time, the test reports will remain valid for the purpose of grant of licence under option – 2?
answer: The test reports of the product shall not generally be more than 90 days old. For complete details please visit www.bis.gov.in>>Conformity assessment >> Product Certification >> Certification process >>Guideline for Grant of Licence.

question: Q 14. What is the fee applicable for Certification licence for a product?
answer: The application is required to be submitted with an application fee of Rs. 1000. An inspection fee of Rs. 7,000 per man day is required to be paid before preliminary inspection visit by BIS. After evaluation and decision to grant the licence is taken by BIS, the applicant is required to deposit annual licence fee of Rs. 1000 plus the minimum marking fee specified for the product. The marking fee for each product is specified in Annexure I of Scheme I of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 as amended by BIS (Conformity Assessment) Amendment Regulations, 2020.

question: Q 15. What is the timeline for grant of BIS product certification licence?
answer: Average time taken for grant of licence under option-2 is generally one month and under option-1 four months from the date of receipt of complete application and its recording. Itmay vary for reasons like delay in response to queries raised, if any; organizing inspection(s); sample deposition, and fee dues, etc.

question: Q 16. What are the conditions of BIS licence to use or apply a Standard Mark?
answer: Conditions of BIS licence to use or apply a Standard Mark are as given in Regulation 6 of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018

question: Q 18. What is the validity of BIS product certification licence?
answer: BIS certification under Scheme-I may be granted initially upto two years which is valid only for the varieties mentioned in the licence. For extension of validity, application with requisite fee and documents under the existing licence is required to be submitted. Licence may be renewed up to five years from the last date of validity of licence.

question: Q 19. How should one apply for the renewal of a licence?
answer: Renewal of licence is required to be requested through online portal “manakonline” and is available through dashboard of the licence holder. Renewal application with production details for the relevant period (to calculate the actual marking fee), and the relevant fee is required to be submitted through online for renewal as per the period of renewal opted.

question: Q.2 I am a manufacturer of a product and interested in applying for BIS product certification licence. How should I apply for it when I am not aware of corresponding Indian Standard Number?
answer: You can search for the Indian Standard against a product at the URL:https://www.manakonline.in/MANAK/ApplicationLicenceRelatedrptIf you cannot find the relevant Indian Standard, send a query to concerned technical department of BIS athttps://www.bis.gov.in/php/BIS/biswebsite/standards/technical-departments/.

question: Q 20. What is deferment of licence? When does it happen?
answer: The renewal of licence can be deferred as per provision of Regulation 8 of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, if the renewal application and fee is not received till the last date of validity of licence or if the licence is under suspension.

question: Q 21. Does BIS carry any surveillance on my licence regularly?
answer: After grant of licence to a manufacturer, BIS carries out surprise factory surveillance inspections through visit to the factory by certification officers of BIS or by personnel of the Agents appointed by BIS as per Rule 33 of BIS Rules, 2018. During such visits, it is verified that the manufacturer continues to maintain the manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities and conformity of the product to the relevant standard(s). Testing of the product samples in factory is also witnessed during such visits.Sample of ISI marked product is also drawn from the factory for verifying conformity to relevant ISS through third party laboratory testing. BIS also carries out market surveillance through purchase of samples of ISI marked product for verifying conformity of the product to relevant ISS through third party laboratory testing.

question: Q 22. What are the duties and responsibilities of the owner of a manufacturing unit holding BIS licence regarding factory surveillance?
answer: BIS licence holder is required to extend co-operation to the certification officers of BIS or personnel of the agents appointed by BIS to carry out surveillance inspection. The licence holder shall also share relevant records and information sought . He would also facilitate testing in the factory and drawl of samples for independent testing in third party lab. The licence holder shall be required to deposit samples to the designated laboratory as per advice of the officer

question: Q 23. What are the consequences of non-cooperation by the manufacturing unit during factory surveillance
answer: No, one licence is granted by BIS for one product/one Indian Standard (however, the licence may cover more than one variety/grade/size etc. specified/covered in the standard). The products and its varieties on which Standard Mark can be used is mentioned in the “Scope of licence” granted to you. It cannot be used for other product varieties not covered in the scope. However, you can get the scope of licence changed (inclusion or deletion of varieties) with reference to the standard against which licence has been granted and as per applicable relevant guidelines. For change in the existing scope of product licence (addition/ deletion of varieties), please visit:www.bis.gov.in>>Conformity Assessment >>Product Certification >> Certification process >>Guideline for Change in Scope of Licence.

question: Q 24. I have already got licence from BIS for the product as per ISS in my factory. Can I use this licence on all varieties of the product being manufactured in the factory?
answer: No, one licence is granted by BIS for one product/one Indian Standard (however, the licence may cover more than one variety/grade/size etc. specified/covered in the standard). The products and its varieties on which Standard Mark can be used is mentioned in the “Scope of licence” granted to you. It cannot be used for other product varieties not covered in the scope. However, you can get the scope of licence changed (inclusion or deletion of varieties) with reference to the standard against which licence has been granted and as per applicable relevant guidelines.For change in the existing scope of product licence (addition/ deletion of varieties), please visit:www.bis.gov.in>>Conformity Assessment >>Product Certification >> Certification process >>Guideline for Change in Scope of Licence.

question: Q. 25 What is the procedure for intimation regarding change of address or shifting of the manufacturing unit?
answer: BIS licence holder is required to inform BIS of its intentions of shifting of the manufacturing unit to a new address with relevant documents for the new premises similar to the documents submitted at the time of application to BIS for grant of licence. The licensee on its own shall suspend the use of the Standard Mark under intimation to the Bureau on relocation of manufacturing unit to new premises. The revocation of suspension may be done by the Bureau after verification of the old premises and verification of production process at new premises as per provision of paragraph 11 (3) & (4) of scheme I of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: Q. 26 When can a license be suspended?
answer: The licence can be suspended under provisions of paragraph 11 of scheme I and Regulation 10 of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: Q.27 When can a license be cancelled?
answer: The licence can be cancelled under provisions of Regulation 11 of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: Q. 28 How can a BIS licensee participate in the standard formulation/revision process?
answer: The Indian standards are formulated and revised by BIS through consensus in technical committees. BIS licensee can participate in this process by becoming a member of the technical committee and may send comments to the concerned technical department through mail/BIS website. question: Q.3 For which products, the BIS licence is compulsory? Or I am manufacturing a product. Is it compulsory to get BIS licence for my product?
answer: Products are brought under compulsory certification by the Central Government as per the provision of BIS Act, 2016 or other Acts. Detail of products which are covered under compulsory BIS certification is available athttps://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/If your product is in this list, it is compulsory for you to get a BIS licence for it. .

question: Q.4 What are the essential requirements to be possessed by a manufacturer for applying to BIS for obtaining licence?
answer: For obtaining BIS licence, the manufacturer must have requisite manufacturing infrastructure, appropriate process controls, quality control and testing capabilities for the product as per relevant Indian Standard (ISS). The product shall also conform to all requirements laid down in the ISS.

question: Q.5 How BIS grants the licence?
answer: The Bureau grants the licence based on successful assessment of the manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, quality control and testing capabilities of the manufacturerthrough a visit to its manufacturing premises. Conformity of the product to the relevant standard(s) is also established through third party laboratory testing or testing in the manufacturing premises or a combination of both.

question: Q.6 What is the procedure for obtaining BIS licence for use of BIS Standard Mark?
answer: There are two options available for obtaining BIS product certification licence under Scheme – I. For details, please see Guidelines for grant of licence

question: Q.7 Where do I submit my application?or How can I apply for getting BIS licence for use of BIS standard mark (ISI) on the product?
answer: A.BIS accepts application for product certification in online mode only (including all payments). To submit your application, please visit our online portal,www.manakonlinein Before registering in the portal, you are advised to go through applicant user manual, FAQs related to portal athttps://www.manakonline.in/MANAK/impLinks

question: Q.8 Are there any technical guidelines available for the products under Product Certification Scheme of BIS?
answer: Yes, the technical guidelines are available for all the products covered under Product Certification Scheme as ‘Product Manuals’. Product manuals include sampling guidelines, list of test equipments, Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), description of scope etc. To search the desired Product Manual, please follows the web link: www.bis.gov.in>> Conformity Assessment >> Product Certification>> Product Specific Guidelines >> Product Manuals.

question: Q.9 If product specific guidelines i.e. Product Manual, SIT, grouping guidelines and/or marking fee rate for my product is not defined, will I still be able to obtain a BIS licence?
answer: In case product specific guidelines and/or marking fee for your product is not defined, it is possible that you are the first manufacturer to apply for a BIS licence for new product. However, you will still be able to obtain BIS licence as per Scheme I of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulation, 2018. Basic principles and procedure for grant of licence will remain the same in such a case also with specific relaxation as provided in Guidelines for Grant of licence. BIS will interact with you throughout the certification process to define the product specific guidelines and marking fee rate. This will be called ‘All India First Licence’

question: Q17. What are the punitive provisions for non-compliance with the conditions of the licence?
answer: In case of violation of conditions of licence, licence may be cancelled by the Bureau as per provision of Regulation 11 of BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: Should a customer take an authentic bill/invoice for hallmarked jewellery?
answer: Yes. An authentic bill/invoice should be obtained from the jeweller/retailer.

question: What are the current hallmarking charges for gold?
answer: BIS states ₹45 per gold article, with minimum consignment charges of ₹200, plus applicable service tax/other levies.

question: What are the current hallmarking charges for silver?
answer: BIS states ₹35 per silver article, with minimum consignment charges of ₹150, plus applicable service tax/other levies.

question: What are the licensee's responsibilities during factory surveillance?
answer: The licensee must cooperate with BIS officers or authorized surveillance personnel, provide requested records and information, facilitate factory testing and sample drawal, and deposit samples with the designated laboratory when directed.

question: What are the options for obtaining a BIS licence under Scheme-I?
answer: BIS provides two options for obtaining a product-certification licence under Scheme-I. The detailed requirements are given in the Guidelines for Grant of Licence.

question: What are the refinery/A&H-related fees under the Hallmarking Regulations?
answer: BIS's current FAQ lists refinery/mint fee components including ₹10,000 application fee, ₹5,000 renewal application fee, ₹5,000 assessment fee per man-day and ₹60,000 recognition/renewal fee for three years, as applicable to the cited refinery/mint fee structure.
document_reference: BIS Act and Regulation FAQ Q4

question: What benefit does hallmarked jewellery provide to a customer?
answer: It provides third-party assurance and confidence that the customer receives the declared purity/fineness for the price paid.

question: What compensation applies when hallmarked jewellery has lower purity?
answer: BIS states that under Rule 49, for a non-conforming precious-metal article the prescribed compensation, where directed, is two times the shortage amount calculated from the purity difference and article weight plus testing charges.

question: What conditions apply to use of the BIS Standard Mark?
answer: The conditions for use or application of the Standard Mark are those specified in Regulation 6 of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: What control does BIS exercise over jewellers and A&H Centres?
answer: BIS conducts surveillance audits of Assaying & Hallmarking Centres and draws market samples from registered/certified jewellers for testing in BIS referral assay laboratories.

question: What details should be included in the jewellery bill?
answer: The bill should contain details of the hallmarked articles; BIS also states that the description of each article, net precious-metal weight, purity in carat/fineness and hallmarking charges should be included for sale of hallmarked precious-metal articles.

question: What do the BIS Hallmarking Regulations, 2018 cover?
answer: They contain provisions concerning registration of jewellers, recognition of Assaying & Hallmarking Centres and grant of licences for refineries.
document_reference: BIS Act and Regulation FAQ Q3

question: What does a hallmark on gold jewellery consist of?
answer: Since the introduction of HUID on 1 July 2021, the hallmark consists of the BIS logo, purity in caratage/fineness, and six-digit alphanumeric HUID.

question: What hallmark sizes are permitted?
answer: BIS specifies permissible hallmark heights: for gold 1.5, 1.0, 0.75 and 0.5 mm; for silver 4.0, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0 and 0.75 mm.

question: What happens if a licensee violates BIS licence conditions?
answer: BIS may cancel the licence under Regulation 11 of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 for violation of licence conditions.

question: What happens if a sample fails after being tampered with in the supply chain?
answer: Normally the manufacturer/jeweller who obtained hallmarking is held responsible. If the manufacturer alleges tampering during supply, BIS investigates the supply chain and takes action after a thorough enquiry.

question: What happens when an entire lot fails Fire Assaying?
answer: The rejected items are identified in the delivery voucher.

question: What information is provided in an A&H Centre delivery voucher?
answer: The voucher contains A&H Centre details, jeweller details, details of accepted articles including individual weight and quantity, rejected articles, weight of the returned article, cornet weight and scrapping weight.

question: What is a BIS licence?
answer: A BIS licence is a licence granted under Section 13 of the BIS Act, 2016 to use a specified Standard Mark on goods or articles that conform to a standard.
document_reference: BIS Act 2016; Product Certification FAQ Q1

question: What is a detachable part?
answer: It is any part of jewellery that can be easily removed or replaced.

question: What is an Off-Site Centre?
answer: An Off-Site Centre is an extension of a parent A&H Centre. It has the facilities required for A&H Centre operations except the fire-assay facility.

question: What is deferment of a BIS licence?
answer: Renewal may be deferred under Regulation 8 when the renewal application and required fee have not been received by the licence's last validity date, or when the licence is under suspension.

question: What is FMCS?
answer: FMCS is the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme through which a foreign manufacturer can obtain a BIS licence for products other than the electronic and IT products covered through the Registration Scheme.

question: What is hallmarking?
answer: Hallmarking is the accurate determination and official recording of the proportionate precious-metal content in precious-metal articles. Hallmarks serve as official marks indicating purity/fineness.

question: What is HUID?
answer: HUID means Hallmark Unique Identification. It is a six-digit alphanumeric unique number assigned to each hallmarked item and is traceable. Consumers can verify it using the Verify HUID feature in the BIS Care App.

question: What is the BIS certification-licence fee?
answer: The current FAQ states an application fee of ₹1,000, inspection fee of ₹7,000 per man-day, and after the decision to grant the licence, an annual licence fee of ₹1,000 plus the applicable minimum marking fee. Product-specific marking fees are prescribed separately.

question: What is the typical FMCS grant process?
answer: The process involves submission and scrutiny of the application, inspection/assessment, sample drawal, testing, resolution of queries/non-conformities and the final BIS decision on granting the licence. BIS publishes the detailed process flow under FMCS.

question: What liability does an Off-Site Centre have?
answer: Its liability is the same as that of an Assaying & Hallmarking Centre.

question: What must a manufacturer have before applying for a BIS licence?
answer: The manufacturer must have the required manufacturing infrastructure, appropriate process controls, quality-control arrangements and testing capabilities for the product according to the relevant Indian Standard, and the product must comply with the applicable standard.

question: What should a customer look for at a jewellery shop?
answer: The registered/certified jeweller should display the BIS logo with the wording indicating hallmarked jewellery is available, display the BIS registration certificate, keep a minimum 10X magnifying glass to show hallmarks and display the relationship between fineness and caratage.

question: What should I do if the manufacturing unit shifts to a new address?
answer: The licensee must inform BIS and submit documents relating to the new premises similar to those submitted during the original application. The licensee must suspend use of the Standard Mark during relocation, and BIS may revoke suspension after verification of the old/new premises and production process.

question: What subsidy is available for establishing A&H Centres?
answer: BIS states that under the central assistance scheme, subsidy of 30% to 75% of equipment cost may be provided for establishing A&H Centres at deficient locations. The subsidy does not apply to Off-Site Centres.

question: When can a BIS licence be cancelled?
answer: A BIS licence can be cancelled under Regulation 11 of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: When can a BIS licence be suspended?
answer: A BIS licence can be suspended under paragraph 11 of Scheme-I and Regulation 10 of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018.

question: When should an A&H Centre return the cornet?
answer: The A&H Centre should ensure that jewellery/artefacts are hallmarked and kept ready with the cornet for delivery to the client within 48 hours, as provided under IS 15820.

question: Where can I find FMCS fees?
answer: FMCS applicants must use the fee structure published by BIS under the FMCS section.

question: Where can I find the list of BIS-recognized A&H Centres?
answer: BIS provides the list of recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centres through the Hallmarking section and the Manakonline AHC list.

question: Where can I find the list of BIS registered jewellers?
answer: The list is available under the BIS Hallmarking section on the BIS website.

question: Where can the public find hallmarking information?
answer: BIS provides detailed hallmarking information on its website, including regulations, mandatory hallmarking orders, jeweller/A&H Centre procedures, forms and lists of registered jewellers and hallmarking centres.

question: Where do I submit an application for BIS certification?
answer: BIS accepts product-certification applications online, including payments, through Manakonline. Applicants are advised to review the applicant user manual and portal FAQs before registering.

question: Which gold grades can be hallmarked?
answer: Under IS 1417:2016, the permitted gold jewellery/artefact fineness grades are 14K(585), 18K(750), 20K(833), 22K(916), 23K(958) and 24KS(995).

question: Which Indian Standards apply to hallmarking?
answer: BIS identifies IS 1417:2016 for gold/gold-alloy jewellery and artefacts; IS 2112:2014 for silver/silver-alloy jewellery and artefacts; IS 15820:2009 for Assaying & Hallmarking Centres; IS 1418:2009 for gold assay; IS 2113:2014 for silver assay; and IS 17278:2019 for refined gold/silver bars for Good Delivery.

question: Which laboratories' reports are acceptable for a BIS licence under Option-2?
answer: Reports issued by BIS laboratories or BIS-recognized/empanelled laboratories for the relevant product are acceptable. BIS provides an IS-wise laboratory-testing facility search for identifying suitable laboratories.

question: Which precious metals are currently covered by hallmarking in India?
answer: At present, gold and silver are under the Hallmarking system.

question: Which silver grades can be hallmarked?
answer: Under IS 2112:2014, permitted silver jewellery/artefact grades are 800, 835, 900, 925, 970 and 990 fineness.

question: Who can act as an AIR?
answer: The AIR must be an Indian resident and must undertake responsibility for compliance with the BIS Act, Rules, Regulations, licence terms and related undertakings. A suitably authorized senior person of an Indian branch/office can be nominated; otherwise the foreign manufacturer may nominate an AIR using the prescribed format.

question: Who is responsible for compensation if hallmarked precious-metal jewellery is found below declared purity?
answer: Under the BIS Act/Rules provisions cited by BIS, the certified body/licensee or representative can be directed to repair, replace, reprocess or pay compensation. For precious-metal articles, the compensation is two times the amount calculated for the shortage in purity for the weight sold plus testing charges, where BIS directs compensation.

question: Who operates India's Hallmarking Scheme?
answer: BIS operates the Hallmarking Scheme. BIS was identified in 2000 as the agency to operate the scheme and implements it through its network of regional and branch offices.

question: Why was the Hallmarking Scheme introduced?
answer: The objectives are to protect consumers from malpractices concerning gold/silver quality, help develop India as a leading gold market centre and support export competitiveness.
